issue.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

When performing a reshape on a strided tensor, torch.compile with dynamic compilation appears to assume the tensor is contiguous. The key code is:

```python
key = torch.empty_strided((2, 16, 9), (288, 9, 1), device=device).normal_()
reshaped_key = key.reshape(key.shape[0], 8, -1)
reshaped_key + 1
```

Calling contiguous on the key or compiling with dynamic=False avoids the bug. This is significantly reduced from a program where dynamic compilation was triggered automatically, so there was weird behavior around what had been previously compiled in the same context. Hopefully I haven't introduced something invalid while creating the minimal reproducer. I've attached a reproduction script and the log from TORCH_TRACE

[dedicated_log_torch_trace_vw5keozw.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24683689/dedicated_log_torch_trace_vw5keozw.log)
[torch_compile_dynamic_strides_bug.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24683688/torch_compile_dynamic_strides_bug.py)

### Error logs

Huge difference between eager and compiled output (like 10^33)

### Versions

issue.body:
Stack from [ghstack](https://github.com/ezyang/ghstack) (oldest at bottom):
* __->__ #173062

Fix https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/172693
A  mismatch in output strides between eager and compiled execution.

The solution is to symbolically check whether a view is valid by reusing the existing _compute_stride function. If _compute_stride succeeds, we use the layout it computes.

Note that _compute_stride expects SymInt inputs, so I added a small utility to convert SymPy expressions to SymInt. This avoids having to rewrite the function to operate directly on SymPy. Longer term, the vision is to use SymNodes everywhere, but that is not yet a priority.

Note2: this function is still not perfect for unbacked but that a different issue i will handle separately.

issue.body:
Stack from [ghstack](https://github.com/ezyang/ghstack/tree/0.15.0) (oldest at bottom):
* __->__ #193860

(DO NOT REVIEW, COLLECTING ERRORS)


The strides of an unfrozen FlexibleLayout are provisional: freezing can
reorder them (fill order from decide_layout) or pad them (comprehensive
padding), so a stride read whose result outlives the freeze silently
computes wrong indices. Nothing in the API distinguished a harmless peek
from a persisted read, and this has repeatedly caused silent data
corruption: #147828, and most recently #192575, which was introduced
while fixing #172693 and survived review and six months in main.

This PR makes the peek/persist distinction explicit and enforces it.
Review in this order:

1. ir.py: Layout.stride_hint() / IRNode.get_stride_hint() are the
   explicit way to read provisional strides; results must not be
   persisted. FlexibleLayout.stride raises under the new
   config.strict_flexible_layout_strides
   (TORCHINDUCTOR_STRICT_FLEXIBLE_LAYOUT_STRIDES=1, default off),
   mirroring the existing FlexibleLayout.allow_indexing guard.
   ReinterpretView.__post_init__ now asserts (always on) that the base
   layout is frozen, since the view's FixedLayout indexes raw storage
   and cannot survive a base stride change. Every in-tree producer
   already froze the base except the sites fixed next.
2. Freeze fixes for reads that persist strides: the slice_/select
   unbacked lowerings persist strides/offset into
   DynamicSelectStorageOffset and as_strided views (now frozen via the
   new ir.freeze_storage_layout, which sees through generic views such
   as PermuteView); TMADescriptor's ownership ReinterpretView could
   alias a live FlexibleLayout under
   triton_kernel_default_layout_constraint="flexible_layout"; the
   qlinear binary "sum" lowering re-labels its result as a view of the
   in-place-updated x2.
3. Hint migrations for legitimate peeks: layout predicates
   (is_contiguous, is_stride_ordered, __eq__, storage_size, repr, free
   symbol collection), require_stride1 (some stride == 1 survives any
   freeze), Reduction.num_splits (deliberately compares pre/post-freeze
   strides), the bucketize/searchsorted helpers (their inner_fn is
   re-traced after finalize, so only frozen strides reach kernels), and
   autotune benchmark input generation and mm/bmm template heuristics.
4. clone_preserve_reinterpret_view is deleted: dead code that violated
   the ReinterpretView invariant.

The only default-on behavior change is the ReinterpretView assert. The
strict mode is intended for a CI shard once it has soaked; with it
enabled, the reverted #192575 fix and an untested
TMA-with-flexible-layout case both fail at compile time instead of
silently corrupting results.

Test Plan:

New tests: guard and strict-mode unit tests, a hardened #192575
regression test that pins the padding config and asserts padding fired,
unbacked select/slice with padding_stride_threshold=0, and a strict
end-to-end compile:

```
python test/inductor/test_layout_freezing.py
```

Strict-mode soak (all pass; only failures are pre-existing ones
unrelated to this change, verified against the unpatched tree):

```
TORCHINDUCTOR_STRICT_FLEXIBLE_LAYOUT_STRIDES=1 python -m pytest test/inductor/test_torchinductor.py -k "view or reshape or slice or chunk or split or cat or permute or transpose"
TORCHINDUCTOR_STRICT_FLEXIBLE_LAYOUT_STRIDES=1 python -m pytest test/inductor/test_unbacked_symints.py test/inductor/test_padding.py test/inductor/test_max_autotune.py test/inductor/test_triton_kernels.py
```

Default-mode soak:

```
python -m pytest test/inductor/test_torchinductor.py test/inductor/test_max_autotune.py test/inductor/test_triton_kernels.py
```

The qlinear binary path could not be exercised locally (local build has
no onednn); relying on CI for that path.

Written with Claude Code.
